chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAlī ibn Ismāʿīl, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Ibn Miskān, from al-Ḥārith ibn al-Mughīrah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), who said:

I heard him saying: The Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) said: We, in the matter, and understanding, and the halal, and the haram, proceed in one single course. But as for the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) and ʿAlī (عليه السلام), they have their own excellence.

key_terms.الْأَمْرِ: the divinely vested authority or command
key_terms.الْحَرَامِ: what is forbidden in the Sacred Law
key_terms.الْحَلَالِ: what is permissible in the Sacred Law
key_terms.الْفَهْمِ: understanding in religious knowledge and guidance
key_terms.مَجْرًى وَاحِدًا: in one single course or unified path

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the shared authority of the Imams and the special excellence of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) and ʿAlī (عليه السلام)?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the Divine Guides share one course in authority concerning command, understanding, and the clarification of halal and haram. It also affirms a distinct excellence for the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) and ʿAlī (عليه السلام).
